Note: Unmatched Labs health dial. MeshURL and DiffuseURL are filled in on export - the mesh is generated (a 50.8mm disc) and the diffuse is the face art. To use this file on its own, point MeshURL at a disc and DiffuseURL at a square picture.

ObjectStates.Name: Custom_Model
ObjectStates.Description: Click a trigger to change the health; click the number, or alt-click a trigger, to reset it.
ObjectStates.LuaScript:
--[[
  Health dial — Unmatched Labs.

  The disc itself is plain. Everything a player reads on it is drawn from here,
  as three buttons on its top face: the current health in the middle, and a
  trigger either side of it. Left-click a trigger to move the count by one;
  click the number itself, or alt-click a trigger, to put the dial back to full.

  Positions are in the model's own units, which are inches, and were laid out
  against a two-inch disc — the triggers sit at 0.6 of its one-inch radius. A
  disc cut to another size needs them moved to match.

  Two rules about TTS buttons cost five rounds between them, and neither can be
  tested outside the game. Leave both alone unless the game says otherwise.

  1. A BUTTON WITH A TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND DRAWS NO LABEL.

     Not a faint label — none, while the button stays perfectly clickable, with
     a working tooltip. Set `color`'s alpha to nought and the text is simply not
     there. That is where the number went three times, and it is why the arrows
     were never visible once in any version of this script: they were drawn on a
     clear background from the very first draft, which looked like the tidy
     thing to do.

     So every button here is given a plate. `PLATE_ALPHA` is the one knob; take
     it to nought and you get a dial with three invisible controls, which is a
     working dial that looks broken.

  2. `draw` MUST NOT CALL `self.clearButtons()`.

     Clearing and creating in the same frame takes the new buttons along with
     the old. The dial spawns bare, all three missing. `draw` runs once, from
     `onLoad`, so there has never been anything to clear.

  A third thing is merely good practice: nothing in `draw` may throw. The
  buttons are made in one pass, so an error in the first takes the other two
  with it and the object looks like a plain disc with no explanation. The
  model's bounds are read through a pcall and the tooltips are built from CONFIG
  alone.

  The table below is rewritten by the workshop's exporter, which reads it a line
  at a time rather than as Lua. Keep every entry a plain scalar on a line of its
  own, and keep the closing brace in the first column.
]]

CONFIG = {
    MIN_VALUE = 0,
    MAX_VALUE = 20,
    VALUE = 20,
    NUMBER_SIZE = 300,
    TRIGGER_SIZE = 300,
    INK = "ffffff",
    PLATE = "1a1a1a",
    PLATE_ALPHA = 1,
    SHOW_TOOLTIP = true,
}

-- Where a trigger sits, as a share of the disc's radius.
local TRIGGER_X = 0.6

--[[ Button units to one of the model's inches, read off the game rather than
     guessed: a label set at 600 drew its figures 0.857in tall on the two-inch
     disc. So a font size is about 700 to the inch, and 300 sets two figures
     0.62in across and 0.43in tall — inside the 0.80in circle the skin template
     marks for them. ]]
local PER_INCH = 700

local function clamp(value)
    if value < CONFIG.MIN_VALUE then return CONFIG.MIN_VALUE end
    if value > CONFIG.MAX_VALUE then return CONFIG.MAX_VALUE end
    return value
end

--[[ A hex colour, as the button API wants it: nought to one, and named.

     `a = 1` is fully opaque, not 100. TTS clamps anything above one, so a
     script written against a 0..100 range appears to work while quietly having
     no way to ask for anything but solid. ]]
local function colour(hex, alpha)
    local digits = string.gsub(hex, "#", "")
    return {
        r = tonumber(string.sub(digits, 1, 2), 16) / 255,
        g = tonumber(string.sub(digits, 3, 4), 16) / 255,
        b = tonumber(string.sub(digits, 5, 6), 16) / 255,
        a = alpha
    }
end

local function ink() return colour(CONFIG.INK, 1) end

--[[ The plate every button sits on. It is not decoration: see rule 1 above —
     with no plate there is no label either. It earns its place regardless,
     keeping white type readable over whatever picture the dial is wearing, and
     the three line up at one height so they read as a control rather than as
     boxes that happen to be there. ]]
local function plate() return colour(CONFIG.PLATE, CONFIG.PLATE_ALPHA) end

--[[ A rect, given in inches, because everything else about this dial is.

     A label is laid out *inside* its rect and whatever does not fit is not
     drawn, so a rect has to be comfortably bigger than the label it holds —
     these carry about 1.4x the ink across and 1.4x the font size down.

     They must also not reach each other: where two rects overlap, the button
     made first takes the click, and a number sized generously enough to draw
     once covered both triggers and stopped them answering. The number spans
     x -0.43..0.43 and a trigger 0.45..0.75. ]]
local function rect(wide, tall)
    return wide * PER_INCH, tall * PER_INCH
end

--[[ The buttons float just clear of the top face. The thickness is read off the
     model rather than assumed, so a disc cut thicker does not swallow them —
     but a Custom_Model may not have its mesh yet, so a failure here falls back
     to the 2mm the workshop actually generates, in inches. ]]
local function faceY()
    local ok, bounds = pcall(function() return self.getBoundsNormalized() end)
    if ok and bounds ~= nil and bounds.size ~= nil and bounds.size.y ~= nil then
        return bounds.size.y / 2 + 0.02
    end
    return 0.06
end

-- Built from CONFIG alone. `self.getName()` is one more thing that can be nil.
local function caption()
    if CONFIG.SHOW_TOOLTIP then
        return CONFIG.VALUE .. " of " .. CONFIG.MAX_VALUE
    end
    return ""
end

local function show()
    self.editButton({ index = 0, label = tostring(CONFIG.VALUE), tooltip = caption() })
end

local function step(by, alt)
    if alt then
        CONFIG.VALUE = CONFIG.MAX_VALUE
    else
        CONFIG.VALUE = clamp(CONFIG.VALUE + by)
    end
    show()
end

--[[ A trigger. Its glyph is drawn by the button rather than painted onto the
     face, so it stays put whatever picture the dial is wearing. ]]
local function trigger(handler, glyph, x, y, verb)
    local width, height = rect(0.30, 0.60)
    self.createButton({
        click_function = handler,
        function_owner = self,
        label = glyph,
        tooltip = verb .. " — alt-click for full",
        position = { x, y, 0 },
        width = width,
        height = height,
        alignment = 3,
        font_size = CONFIG.TRIGGER_SIZE,
        font_color = ink(),
        color = plate()
    })
end

function draw()
    local y = faceY()

    --[[ The count, and the middle of the dial as its target: clicking it
         resets. The rect is the number zone the skin template draws, which
         holds the two figures a 0..99 range can reach with room to spare. It is
         button 0, which is the index `show` edits, so it is made first. ]]
    local width, height = rect(0.86, 0.60)
    self.createButton({
        click_function = "reset",
        function_owner = self,
        label = tostring(CONFIG.VALUE),
        tooltip = caption(),
        position = { 0, y, 0 },
        width = width,
        height = height,
        alignment = 3,
        font_size = CONFIG.NUMBER_SIZE,
        font_color = ink(),
        color = plate()
    })

    trigger("lower", "<", -TRIGGER_X, y, "Lose one")
    trigger("raise", ">", TRIGGER_X, y, "Gain one")
end

function onSave()
    return JSON.encode({ value = CONFIG.VALUE })
end

--[[ Drawn a beat late, on purpose. A Custom_Model fetches its mesh after the
     object exists, and until that lands there are no bounds to place anything
     against — and buttons made before it can be cleared outright when the real
     mesh arrives. ]]
function onLoad(state)
    if state ~= nil and state ~= "" then
        local ok, saved = pcall(function() return JSON.decode(state) end)
        if ok and saved ~= nil and saved.value ~= nil then
            CONFIG.VALUE = clamp(saved.value)
        end
    end
    Wait.time(draw, 1)
end

function raise(_object, _colour, alt) step(1, alt) end

function lower(_object, _colour, alt) step(-1, alt) end

function reset() step(0, true) end
